methodology.no_edits: Only this new scratchpad artifact written; no tests, schema changes, migrations, provider calls or runtime executions.

CFG-R01.classification: Strong source-derived failure hypothesis, not runtime reproduced
CFG-R01.detail: Creating product with opening stock is two independent requests. Item create is not idempotent; if restock fails after creation, form retains create mode. Retry can create another SKU-less item or hit duplicate SKU instead of resuming stock setup.

CFG-R02.classification: Strong source-derived failure hypothesis, not runtime reproduced
CFG-R02.detail: Multi-email invite form submits sequentially, sets sent results only after whole loop, and inviteStaff supplies no idempotency key. Failure on second email can hide first success; retry repeats first invite and may bill/resend another seat. Backend idempotency support alone does not protect this UI.

CFG-R03.classification: Confirmed expression mismatch; end-user effect needs targeted reproduction
CFG-R03.detail: Editor deposit preview uses Math.round and caps at item price; backend deposit_cents uses Python round for percent and no cap for fixed. Example price=101c percent=50 yields preview=51c versus backend=50c. Fixed deposit exceeding price can preview capped while server returns larger deposit. Tests should define desired rounding/cap policy explicitly.

CFG-R04.detail: useTeam.act sets busyId before request but clears only on success; returned busyId is not masked by action.busy. A rejected role/resend/revoke action may leave row controls busy indefinitely.

CFG-R05.classification: Validation/error-contract weakness from source, no request executed
CFG-R05.detail: ItemUpdate allows explicit null for DB non-null fields; update applies null directly. _save maps every IntegrityError to duplicate-SKU Conflict, so a null name/price/etc may misleadingly return SKU conflict instead of validation. This must be separated from legitimate optional-field clearing.

CRM-R01.title: Client status PATCH bypasses manager archive/restore boundary
CRM-R01.status: Source-supported candidate; no HTTP/DB reproduction performed
CRM-R01.detail: ClientUpdate exposes status; ClientService.update applies it without manager role gate. Staff can appear able to PATCH inactive or active even though archive/restore endpoints reject staff. UI classifies by status and active pickers/returning proof depend on status; this can also leave archived_at inconsistent. Decide whether status editing is intentionally public to members; if not, add role/state enforcement.

CRM-R02.title: Historical timeline may omit visits outside replica window
CRM-R02.status: Source-supported candidate; no UI reproduction performed
CRM-R02.detail: useEarlierVisits requests limit=1 and consumes count/last_completed_at. useClientHistory only reads local CLIENT_VISITS_SQL and never merges older API rows. The existing browser history test asserts HTTP 200, not visible historical visit. If full history is intended, add real old-visit rendering/pagination; otherwise label the window explicitly.

CRM-R03.title: Backend validation is looser than UI
CRM-R03.status: Pure schema acceptance reproduced; persistence/error behavior not executed
CRM-R03.detail: Standalone schema probes accepted whitespace-only client/subject/note text, malformed client email, explicit null client name and status inactive. Creation trims whitespace to empty; update directly assigns nullable fields even when underlying column is NOT NULL. UI rejects blank name/contact and malformed email. Test HTTP status and atomicity before classifying exact failure mode.

CRM-R04.title: Client-photo and supplemental merge policy is unspecified
CRM-R04.status: Source-supported gap; not a confirmed defect
CRM-R04.detail: Files with client parent references are not in CLIENT_REFS nor repointed explicitly, and target custom_fields/preferred_channel remain unchanged. Define which source photo/details should survive merge and add assertion. Do not promise every relationship moves based on CLIENT_REFS comment.

SALE-R01.detail: Gift-only desk settlement bypasses assert_parent_stock: apply_gift_card redeems and calls sync_order directly. Unlike cash/card/Terminal, this may consume a unit reserved by an online pending payment. Manual negative-stock allowance does not negate the intended protection of competing holds.
SALE-R01.reproduce: Reserve final tracked unit via online pending intent, then settle same product desk ticket fully with gift card. Assert intended hold protection and no loss of reserved fulfillment.

SALE-R02.classification: source-derived race hypothesis, not runtime reproduced
SALE-R02.detail: Two already-created orders can be patched to contain the same booking while each locks only its own Order. _link_visits reads Booking without FOR UPDATE; both may pass other-ticket check before the booking pointer is overwritten. Order create is serialized by business numbering, so reproduction must use existing tickets.
SALE-R02.reproduce: Patch two open tickets in separate committed sessions to add same visit behind a barrier; assert one wins and losing order retains no billable link/line.

SALE-R03.classification: source-confirmed durability gap, user impact requires reproduction
SALE-R03.detail: Public cart/contact are stored, but pending order and attempt key are useState/useRef only. Reload after accepted order or lost create response loses recovery identity, may create second stock hold, and cannot resume original intent through normal UI. cancelPayment hides result without canceling provider intent.
SALE-R03.reproduce: Accept order then drop response/reload before payment; submit unchanged cart. Count order/intent/hold and require explicit resume/expiry UX policy.

SALE-R04.detail: Resume stores aggregate deposits under out.id while removeLine removes deposit by booking_id, leaving stale deposit preview when a resumed deposit-bearing visit is removed. Server recalculates saved due, preventing trusting the stale amount but creating UI/payment mismatch.
SALE-R04.reproduce: Hold visit+product with collected deposit, resume, remove visit, verify deposit and due clear before requesting cash/card payment.

SALE-R05.detail: Cash endpoint calls on_payment_succeeded after every returned command response including idempotent replay; Notifier sends directly and has no replay gate. Receipt endpoint records receipt_sent_at before dispatch and ready reminder audits are committed even when safe send swallows provider failure.
SALE-R05.reproduce: Replay cash with same key and inspect email/push count; fail receipt/ready transport, recover and verify visible delivery status plus retry policy rather than assuming timestamp means delivered.

SALE-R06.detail: A zero-total sale can pass _chargeable and record zero cash; ledger status requires covered>0 to call sale paid. This may leave a payment-success UI and active succeeded payment with order still open. No zero-total sale completion assertion found in reviewed suites.
SALE-R06.reproduce: 100% discount or free-item sale, tender zero, inspect state, stock, receipt and ability to close/retry. Define explicit free-sale semantics.

PAY-R01.classification: Reproduced route-validation mismatch; sandbox suite not executed
PAY-R01.detail: Over-refund sandbox request has no Idempotency-Key but expects 409; cross-business request has no key but expects 404. Production endpoint requires key. Isolated real payments_router with dependencies replaced by None returned 422 missing header, without invoking endpoint/DB/provider. Existing backend test already asserts this requirement.
PAY-R01.next_step: Supply distinct valid keys in intended domain-negative sandbox requests; keep separate missing-key test. Then run strict suite before relying on prior green claims.

PAY-R02.detail: _settle_payment checks event account ownership when reconstructing unknown intent, but existing Payment lookup by provider_ref proceeds without an explicit account check. Failure/refund/dispute branches also locate provider references without threading event.account. Current wrong-account success test covers an unrecorded intent only. Genuine Stripe IDs are globally scoped and signatures reduce exploitability; nevertheless validate exact wrong-account behavior for existing records rather than claiming a tested invariant.
PAY-R02.next_step: Signed fixture for existing owned provider_ref but mismatched account should have zero ledger/state/notification effect under agreed trust policy.

PAY-R03.classification: Confirmed query limit; user recovery impact requires browser reproduction
PAY-R03.detail: Refund desk selects only newest 200 succeeded payment/deposit rows and filters/searches in memory. Selected initial ID is resolved only in this truncated set. An otherwise refundable older payment may be unreachable even through direct selection. No API fallback/pagination appears in useRefundDesk.
PAY-R03.next_step: Seed >200 succeeded payments and open/search oldest refundable payment; define supported history contract and add retrieval/paging if required.

PAY-R04.detail: Terminal cleanup cancels discovery but does not call a collection cancellation method when unmounted during collectPaymentMethod. active guards stop subsequent JS confirmation, but outstanding SDK collection may remain active and affect next checkout; retry is disabled after charge starts.
PAY-R04.next_step: Simulated reader: dismiss/background/unmount during collection and reconnect; assert documented SDK cancellation/recovery and no unintended confirmation.

PAY-R05.detail: Saved-method resolver permits active bank_eft and fee calculation detects ACSS, but open_card_payment unconditionally stores method=card. If invoice saved-bank charging is intended through this helper, displayed history/receipts may label a debit as card.
PAY-R05.next_step: Charge an authorized saved bank through each intended entry point and assert stored method, receipt label, pending state and refund behavior.

ENT-R01.detail: Generic package consume and generic gift redemption check stored active state but not expires_at. Package cover checks <=now; sweeper uses <now. Usage can therefore differ at/after expiry before sweep. Late-settled package can activate with expired timestamp. Decide uniform policy then verify all entrypoints and worker races.

ENT-R02.status: Source-supported provider-idempotency risk; no provider execution
ENT-R02.detail: Customer subscription provider key is fixed per business/client/item, ignoring new app attempt. Cancel-and-sell-again is explicitly suggested by UI, but a new sale can replay prior provider create result or disagree on changed payment method parameters while that key is retained, then collide on unique provider_ref. Add a real or realistic fake provider contract test.

ENT-R03.status: Source-supported recovery gap; no browser reproduction
ENT-R03.detail: Wallet action computes attempt key but cancelSubscription drops it. Lost response after successful cancel followed by retry gets already-canceled conflict instead of replaying success. UI can show error despite committed cancellation until sync catches up.

ENT-R04.status: Confirmed different notification call paths; intended parity needs decision
ENT-R04.detail: Cash gift purchase activates through _settle_cash but discards activated gift ID and does not enqueue gift-issued notification. Card webhook activation returns ID to notification path. Cash recipient delivery is not asserted in existing cash test.

ENT-R05.status: Source-supported historical tax risk; not reproduced
ENT-R05.detail: Package purchase payment stores charged amount but _package_tax later reads current item price/tax_class, infers registration by matching total and otherwise backs tax out using current class. Changing item tax_class/price before delayed settlement may misallocate original charge between tax and deferred revenue. Existing test covers registration change, not every catalog term change.

ENT-R06.status: Source-supported display mismatch; not reproduced in browser
ENT-R06.detail: Package wallet next-session value uses current item.price_cents divided by sessions, while ledger consumption uses purchased prepaid value and last-session remainder. Changing catalog price or final odd-cent remainder can make displayed next-session amount disagree with accounting.

ENT-R07.status: Validation policy mismatch requiring explicit contract
ENT-R07.detail: UI gift purchases limit $5–$1000, API accepts any positive integer. Direct purchase loaders also do not check active item or client inactive status, although UI offerings/pickers filter them. Decide whether these are deliberate API capabilities or enforcement gaps before writing expected failures.

FIN-R01.title: End-of-day exclusive boundary drops final microsecond
FIN-R01.status: Production pure helper reproduced; no HTTP/database query executed
FIN-R01.detail: period_bounds returns end date at time.max. _legs and remittance owed use occurred_at < hi, excluding an event exactly at that time. Line-based sales/provincial queries use <= hi and include it. Probe with 2026-12-31 business-local23:59:59.999999 showed < false versus <= true. Prefer next-day midnight exclusive contract; verify all consumers before changing.

FIN-R02.title: Staff-pay YTD uses UTC prefix instead of business-local year
FIN-R02.status: Expression/date mismatch demonstrated; hook/UI not executed
FIN-R02.detail: useEarningApprovals chooses current year in business zone but matches paid_at string prefix. A2027-01-01T01:00:00Z payment is Dec31 locally in Vancouver, yet fails prefix2026. Backend T4A uses business-local year instants, so staff-pay and T4A can disagree near New Year.

FIN-R03.title: Removed payees can disappear with outstanding obligations
FIN-R03.detail: PAYEES_SQL filters status active even when entries exist; totals and selected payees derive from that list. Removing a staff member can hide their pending/approved amounts from staff-pay screen while ledger liability remains. Define whether separate historical/removed payee access is required, then test removal with pending and approved earnings.

FIN-R04.title: Partial date-range filing marks entire calendar period filed
FIN-R04.detail: API accepts arbitrary ended date ranges, but next_due and _period status treat any overlapping return as covering the whole calendar period. A one-day return can make the month look filed and suppress the next due period despite other days remaining. Either constrain range alignment or calculate full coverage; tests should first reproduce current result.

FIN-R05.title: Exported text is not protected from spreadsheet formula interpretation
FIN-R05.status: Source-supported output-safety candidate; no spreadsheet opened
FIN-R05.detail: CSV quoting correctly encodes delimiters but raw item/payee names beginning =,+,-,@ pass to writer. Opening in a spreadsheet may interpret them as formulas. Add intentionally harmless formula-shaped names and agree sanitization/export policy; distinguish data fidelity from active-cell interpretation.

FIN-R06.title: Income export and visible income summary may be mistaken for same metric
FIN-R06.status: Confirmed different implementation definitions; product labeling question
FIN-R06.detail: Summary income uses recognized revenue; income.csv uses money received. With unpaid issued invoice, deposits, gift-card sales or tax/tips, expected values differ. Do not assert equality blindly; label/export both concepts consistently or explicitly document intended difference.

FIN-R07.title: Ledger payout report labels any not-failed payout paid
FIN-R07.status: Source-supported status candidate; no pending-payout report run
FIN-R07.detail: ReportService.payouts sets paid unless failed reversal exists, while ledger posts payout movement upon creation. A pending/in-transit provider payout can appear paid in this ledger report, separate from provider-backed payout history. Verify intended meaning and avoid asserting cash arrived solely from this report.

MSG-R01.title: Manual failure looks like successful submit
MSG-R01.status: Source-supported candidate or policy gap; no runtime reproduction
MSG-R01.detail: Backend returns200 status=failed; thread/new-message composers treat resolved promise as success and clear body/attempt. Failure badge may appear later via replica, but user recovery and retained draft are not tested.

MSG-R02.title: Suppression can become stale before send
MSG-R02.status: Source-supported candidate or policy gap; no runtime reproduction
MSG-R02.detail: Broadcast captures targets/contact/locale once and does not re-evaluate consent/STOP/active status before each dispatch. Durable Delivery stores SMS destination and dispatches without consulting current consent. A STOP after snapshot/enqueue can therefore be bypassed unless product deliberately defines a snapshot policy.

MSG-R03.title: Manual provider acceptance before commit
MSG-R03.status: Source-supported candidate or policy gap; no runtime reproduction
MSG-R03.detail: Manual dispatch occurs inside DB transaction without a durable precommitted send claim/provider idempotency key. If provider accepts then DB transaction rolls back or process dies, retry can send again while no durable message records first acceptance. Concurrent first messages also race open_thread unique insert and may surface raw integrity error.

MSG-R04.title: Push success ignores individual provider failures
MSG-R04.status: Source-supported candidate or policy gap; no runtime reproduction
MSG-R04.detail: Expo adapter treats HTTP2xx as success and does not inspect per-message error tickets or fetch receipts. Invalid token/provider error in a successful envelope may remain accepted and token is retained until generic60-day prune. Verify with deterministic provider envelope before real-device smoke.

MSG-R05.title: UI audience differs from server audience
MSG-R05.status: Source-supported candidate or policy gap; no runtime reproduction
MSG-R05.detail: UI counts all eligible-looking contacts; server normalizes SMS contacts and caps500. More than500 or malformed legacy phones can produce preview/result mismatch. Current excluded label describes no consent/contact, not cap.

MSG-R06.title: Long fanout crosses quiet hours or membership change
MSG-R06.status: Source-supported candidate or policy gap; no runtime reproduction
MSG-R06.detail: Quiet-hour/serving checks occur at run start, not each recipient. Slow fanout can continue after21:00 or after business serving status changes. Define intended stop/resume policy and reproduce with a controllable clock and blocked adapter.

DOC-R01.detail: Provider Forms exposes response counts but no reviewed answer/signature reader. Historical definition/signature are omitted from response sync projection. Baseline provider-reads-response happy path cannot currently be assumed implemented.
DOC-R01.next_step: Define response viewing/export contract and access policy; verify actual UI inability and add capability before relying on E2E completion.

DOC-R02.classification: Focused schema acceptance reproduced; persistence unexecuted
DOC-R02.detail: PublicContractSign accepts typed_name containing only spaces; sign strips it to empty without post-strip validation. PublicFileCreate and FileCreate accept size=-1; public upload checks only None/upper bound.
DOC-R02.next_step: API calls must reject blank signer and negative size before status/evidence/file rows change. Schema probe imported production models only, no DB/provider.

DOC-R03.detail: Public form upload/complete has no submitted-state check; same bearer token can mint more uploads after submission. Presigned PUT remains usable after confirmation/submission, so uploaded attachment bytes may be replaceable until URL expiry; confirm does not re-HEAD once uploaded_at set.
DOC-R03.next_step: Define post-submission upload and evidence immutability policy. Test completed-token upload and same-key overwrite through still-valid PUT; do not assume uploaded metadata guarantees immutable bytes.

DOC-R04.detail: New idempotency key generated each UI create/send attempt; lost response can create another form/contract/request. Upload hook supplies no key. Contract direct notifier is inside database command but external send can succeed before rollback or be swallowed and permanently skipped on same-key replay.
DOC-R04.next_step: Drop response after commit then retry without editing; inspect object and message counts. Fault after external send before commit, define recovery evidence.

DOC-R05.detail: Intake query has no row claim/client-form uniqueness, so two runs may create duplicate responses/send. Pending-file pruner does not lock/filter again at delete, so concurrent completion may race deletion. Person photo replacement does not lock parent and deletes other pending as well as uploaded photos.
DOC-R05.next_step: Barrier-controlled committed worker/complete/replace races, checking actual rows, accessible objects and notification counts.

DOC-R06.detail: Generic subject/signature/form_response parent IDs are not validated by FileService.create; booking complete checks tenant but not current booking assignment. Public-media allowed-purpose uploads do not restrict content to images server-side. These are integrity/permission boundary questions, not proof of arbitrary cross-tenant read.
DOC-R06.next_step: Test foreign/missing generic parents, completion after reassignment/removal, and HTML/octet-stream labelled public image; define valid parent-purpose-content matrix.

DOC-R07.detail: Private image cache expiry is checked only when api/IDs effect runs, no refresh timer. Constant mounted photo can retain expired URL. Public contract hook maps any status other than signed/declined to pending, including expired. No expiry job/TTL found for contracts/forms.
DOC-R07.next_step: Keep photo mounted past link TTL; test explicit expired signature row. Decide supported expiry lifecycle rather than inventing expired-token behavior.

REV-R01.classification: Source-supported eligibility inconsistency, not runtime reproduced
REV-R01.detail: Automatic job variable active selects nondeleted Client IDs but does not require status active. Archive endpoint uses inactive+archived_at; existing archived test only sets deleted_at. Therefore an actually archived client with recent completed visit may receive automatic request even though UI suggestions exclude them. Manual no-booking request also permits nondeleted inactive client; define manual policy separately.
REV-R01.next_step: Archive through real endpoint, execute job at eligible time, assert intended request/delivery suppression; add true archive test without substituting deleted_at.

REV-R02.classification: Source-supported recovery gap; no browser reproduction
REV-R02.detail: useRequestReview generates fresh key for every click. If request/queue commits and response is lost, retry receives cooldown/booking-duplicate error rather than replaying successful result. Backend prevents duplicate work but UI may report failure despite recorded request.
REV-R02.next_step: Drop response after commit; retry, then assert existing request is surfaced and no duplicate queue. Decide whether stable attempt key or recovery lookup is appropriate.

REV-R03.detail: Global lapsed-plan write gate does not allow Google disconnect, so expired business can be blocked from removing local provider access. Conversely already queued reply worker checks actor and connection but not plan access, unlike automatic invitation job. This may be intentional in-flight completion, but needs explicit policy and UI evidence.
REV-R03.next_step: Lapse with active profile and queued operation; check disconnect/reconnect/reply and worker behavior against agreed policy.

REV-R04.classification: Confirmed memory-only flow boundary; user impact unexecuted
REV-R04.detail: OAuth handle lives only in pending async hook closure. Reload/unmount/business switch invalidates polling while popup may complete server callback; returning page has no stored handle to finalize credentials. Native kill/resume similarly needs explicit restart flow. Callback-completed handle TTL is at most two minutes, shorter than initial ten-minute flow.
REV-R04.next_step: Reload parent or terminate native after provider callback; assert safe retry/recovery and no wrong-session credential attachment.

REV-R05.classification: Source-supported versioned command recovery boundary; unexecuted
REV-R05.detail: Frontend sends idempotency keys for location selection/disconnect but those routes do not consume them. Successful selection increments generation; lost response then retry with old generation returns stale conflict. Disconnect already-disconnected is effectively idempotent, but profile selection requires reload/recovery.
REV-R05.next_step: Drop select response after commit and retry; UI should read current connection and recover rather than imply selection failed.

PLN-R01.status: Source-supported recovery gap; no runtime reproduction
PLN-R01.detail: GET plan fetches current subscription, but access/plan_status still come from local Business; the seat sync job adjusts quantity without mirroring status. A missed cancellation/unpaid webhook may leave stale writable local access even after Refresh. Define repair through reconciliation or status refresh and test event withheld then recovery.

PLN-R02.detail: Resending expired Premium invite can increase provider seats before email. Unlike create_invite, resend lacks exception compensation. Email failure rolls back fresh invitation timestamp while external quantity can remain high until daily sync; a stable count retry may mask temporary extra prorations.

PLN-R03.status: Confirmed gate scope; intended recovery policy needs decision
PLN-R03.detail: Lapsed allowlist permits refunds/removal but not Google disconnect or cancellation of client subscriptions. Existing queued Google replies can continue, and external recurring customer subscriptions remain separate. Decide whether disabling external actions/stopping future charges must remain available; then assert these actual valid requests, not merely generic gate enumeration.

PLN-R04.detail: live_invite requires invited_at>now-seven-days, so equality is unbilled; _pending expires only when invited_at+TTL<now, so equality remains acceptable. Invite can be valid at an instant it no longer reserves/bills a seat. Accept rechecks cap, limiting overcapacity, but expiry and price semantics differ.

PLN-R05.detail: usePlanAccess computes time during render without a timer. A stationary app may retain trial banner/access presentation across deadline until another update, while server correctly refuses writes. Web plan page also lacks native focus-refresh behavior when returning via browser history.

PLN-R06.detail: close_plan_checkouts reads at most100 open and10 completed sessions with .data; duplicate refund helper reads100 invoices and100 invoice payments without pagination. Normal use may stay below limits, but claims of exhaustive duplicate cleanup need explicit bounds/tests.

SYN-R01.status: Source-supported expiry-refresh question; no runtime reproduction
SYN-R01.detail: useHistoryRange evaluates23-hour marker expiry during render without a dedicated expiry timer. Its schedule consumer also calls useNow, which may provide rerenders, so this is not a confirmed stale-view bug. Exercise a long-lived offline schedule at expiry and future consumers that lack incidental ticks.

SYN-R02.status: Confirmed ephemeral state; end-to-end safety needs evidence
SYN-R02.detail: Arrival expectations disappear on reload and after120 seconds. Correctness must come from authoritative command/idempotency/domain invariants, not this indicator. Delay replication across reload and verify actual effects for high-risk features.

SYN-R03.status: Platform durability and authorization limit, not an asserted implementation defect
SYN-R03.detail: Storage persistence denial is ignored and browser/OS eviction remains possible. Offline identities may access cached data until the seven-day limit without learning remote revocation. Product wording and recovery tests must reflect these explicit limits.

SYN-R04.detail: Real service specs skip when endpoint absent. CI should call the isolated verification wrapper and assert required spec execution, not infer full sync coverage from a generic package command.

OPS-R01.title: Business delivery failures lack this admin viewer
OPS-R01.status: Source-supported candidate or policy boundary; not runtime reproduced
OPS-R01.detail: Admin deliveries filters admin: keys; normal queued/failed/ambiguous client notifications are absent. Operations has no worker heartbeat or retry actions. This is a capability/observability gap, not proof that workers fail.
OPS-R01.next_step: Define supported operations surface and add scenario where ordinary receipt is ambiguous/failed and operator can identify it through the intended tooling.

OPS-R02.title: Restricted test key selects live Stripe dashboard link
OPS-R02.status: Source-supported candidate or policy boundary; not runtime reproduced
OPS-R02.detail: Payment detail infers test mode only with stripe_secret_key.startswith(sk_test_). An rk_test_ configuration is not recognized and produces path without test/.
OPS-R02.next_step: Unit/API fixture with restricted test key, then verify link URL and account scope; prefer explicit mode or robust supported prefix policy.

OPS-R03.title: Contact success has no durable recovery
OPS-R03.status: Source-supported candidate or policy boundary; not runtime reproduced
OPS-R03.detail: Contact sends directly and returns thanks when send accepts. Lost303 response or DB-independent retry can duplicate mail; accepted provider message has no persisted delivery record. Waitlist confirmation failure similarly logs and still thanks without durable retry.
OPS-R03.next_step: Fault after provider acceptance and before response; define whether at-least-once contact and best-effort confirmation are acceptable and assert clear retry behavior.

OPS-R04.title: Waitlist contact proxy may collapse visitor rate identities
OPS-R04.status: Source-supported candidate or policy boundary; not runtime reproduced
OPS-R04.detail: Node apiContact forwards form but not original client IP. Backend contact rate limiter observes proxy/server origin; many unrelated visitors may share backend quota. Node trusts first X-Forwarded-For for its own per-address limit, unlike configured backend proxy-hop logic.
OPS-R04.next_step: Integration with realistic trusted proxy headers and two visitor IPs; verify rate isolation, spoof refusal and failure-page behavior without contacting real users.

OPS-R05.title: Detail evidence truncation can look complete
OPS-R05.status: Source-supported candidate or policy boundary; not runtime reproduced
OPS-R05.detail: Admin payment refund/ledger arrays and person/business detail arrays stop at100 with no pagination field in detail. A heavily active record may omit earlier evidence needed to reconcile history.
OPS-R05.next_step: Seed >100 related records, inspect latest/oldest and ensure explicit limit/next retrieval policy. Do not silently claim whole-account reconciliation from bounded panel.

OPS-R06.title: Platform admin does not require enrollment in MFA by its own gate
OPS-R06.status: Source-supported candidate or policy boundary; not runtime reproduced
OPS-R06.detail: assert_platform_access verifies allowlist+email only; second_factor is informational. Kratos highest_available protects enrolled accounts but may allow an allowlisted account with no second factor.
OPS-R06.next_step: Decide mandatory-enrollment policy; test allowed verified identities with and without enrolled second factor through deployed login and direct API. Do not describe this as bypass of an existing explicit requirement.
